prompt:
Architectural floor plan of one room, drawn straight from above as a clean top-down orthographic plan view in the style of a set designer's ground plan: white background, thick dark walls with gaps for doors and windows, door swings drawn as arcs, windows as thin double lines, and every piece of furniture as a simple outline from above, to scale. In the plan, its bottom edge is the front wall, its top edge the back wall, its left edge the left wall and its right edge the right wall, as the establishing view names them. Draw only the doors, windows and openings the description names. Location: Jail, a cell. A narrow, present-day concrete jail cell painted dull grey-green, with a scuffed grey concrete floor. Back wall: a small high rectangular window with steel bars, through which a pale shaft of daylight slants down into the cell. Left wall: a steel bunk bolted lengthwise along the wall, with a thin grey mattress, a folded grey wool blanket and a flat pillow. Right wall: the barred steel cell door, the only way in, which opens onto a dim corridor; beside it in the back-right corner stands a stainless-steel toilet-sink unit. Front wall (behind the camera): bare concrete with a small steel shelf. A caged fluorescent tube on the ceiling gives a flat, cold white top light.

Avoid: people, text, labels, numbers, letters, dimensions, compass, logos, watermark, a door or window the description does not name.
